newsitem.title: INDIA: Lehman sees profit rise at India's VSNL.
newsitem.headline: Lehman sees profit rise at India's VSNL.

text.p: Investment bank Lehman Brothers said on Monday that it expects Indian telecommunications firm Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) to post average annual profit growth of 25 percent over the next five years.
Lehman Brothers said in a statement released in India that "strong unit growth and steady margins are expected to lead to annual profit growth averaging 25 percent for the next five years".
The investment bank announced that it has initiated coverage of VSNL with a 2-Outperform rating and recommended VSNL as a core holding in an Indian portfolio.
Lehman Brothers said it set a 12-month share price target of 1,650 rupees. On August 30, VSNL shares closed at 1,150 rupees on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
"VSNL's net cash position and strong balance sheet make it one of the strongest balance sheets of all Indian corporates," Lehman Brothers said.
VSNL is a state-run agency which controls overseas telecommunications services from India.

The investment bank said it expects VSNL's traffic to grow at slightly more than 20 percent for the next five years, and it forecast 22 percent average annual growth in revenue for the next five years.
"VSNL will continue to be well placed for the future as further expansion plans can be met by the strong cash flows and borrowings," it said.
